text:
maria (PM): Quick sync — customers keep asking for richer multi-step toolflows where a single API call can trigger multiple tool invocations. Need a decision for the roadmap: ordering guarantees, retry semantics, and circuit-breaker/backpressure behavior. Thoughts? :eyes:

kevin (eng): I think we should define 3 explicit modes in the API: `sequential` (strict ordering), `parallel_ordered` (invoke in parallel but outputs merged/ordered), and `parallel_best_effort` (fan-out, return as available). Each has different perf/cost tradeoffs. Key: require idempotent tool contracts or provide request-id for dedupe.

sanjay (infra): +1 on modes. Infra constraints: parallel_ordered still needs per-invocation KV-cache consistency and may blow up memory if many parallel chains keep KV caches warm. We should add per-route circuit breakers: e.g., fail fast when concurrent tool invocations > N or error-rate > X%. Also introduce a retry budget per root request (e.g., max_retries=2, budget consumed on 429/5xx).

elaine (prodops): For SLAs we need defaults by deployment tier. Hosted: stricter defaults (shorter timeouts, conservative concurrency). Dedicated/Private: expose tunables but warn about cost. Also support `X-Request-Priority` header so customers can opt high-priority traffic through smaller queues.

olivia (design): From a UX perspective interactive chat needs latency predictability. Recommend default `sequential` for `chat.completions` tool-calls, but allow `parallel_ordered` for batch workflows. Example API param idea: { "call_strategy": "sequential", "priority": "normal", "retry_budget": 1 } — want this to be simple. :simple_smile:

kevin (eng): Proposal pseudocode for semantics: 
```
POST /v1/invoke
body: { prompt, tools: [...], call_strategy: "parallel_ordered", retry_budget:2 }
on request:
  allocate_per_request_budget();
  for tool in tools: start_invocation(tool) // parallel
  if call_strategy == "parallel_ordered": collect all results, then order by user-specified ordering
  if errors > budget -> apply circuit-breaker -> fallback to lighter model or return partial with `partial=true`
```
Fallbacks: `fallback_model`, `partial=true`, `retry_after` header.

sanjay (infra): Need observability hooks: per-tool span ids, per-root trace-id, token/cost attribution per tool invocation. Rollout: start with internal alpha on Dedicated, measure memory and latency, then host. Canary gating: block-wide if tail-latency > target.

deploy-bot: Document draft uploaded -> <https://redwood-internal/docs/pipeline-invoke|pipeline invoke spec draft> :page_facing_up:

maria (PM): Good discussion. For prioritization: propose we make the API modes a Q2 initiative, with launch criteria: unit + integration tests for semantics, perf benches showing cost/latency for small/medium/large fanouts, docs + migration guide for existing tool-calling customers, and an enterprise toggle for Dedicated/Private. Who owns what? Timeline suggestions?

kevin (eng): I can own the reference implementation + perf tests. Target: proto in 6 weeks, perf run week 8. :thumbsup:

elaine (prodops): I'll own rollout checklist, SLA matrix, and enterprise toggles. Will draft gating criteria for canary and postmortem playbook.

olivia (design): I will create API naming options and three UX examples (chat, batch ETL, LLM-agents) and short docs snippets.

maria (PM): Great — I'll consolidate into a decision doc and add to the roadmap. Action items: kevin proto, elaine gating, olivia API UX. Meeting next Tues to review proto. :calendar:
